sub_chapter_briefs.title: 2 A.M. on 7.850
sub_chapter_briefs.beat: Mara is at her receiver in the pre-dawn dark, running her nightly scan of dead frequencies, when a repeating pattern surfaces on 7.850 MHz — a frequency she has logged as silent for six years. She freezes, hand on the tuning dial, and listens.
sub_chapter_briefs.brief: Mara is at her receiver in the pre-dawn dark, running her nightly scan of dead frequencies, when a repeating pattern surfaces on 7.850 MHz — a frequency she has logged as silent for six years. She freezes, hand on the tuning dial, and listens.
sub_chapter_briefs.arc_beat: Stage 2 — Call to Adventure: the signal arrives, undeniable and impossible
sub_chapter_briefs.setting: Mara's fortified farmhouse — the radio room, a converted pantry lined with salvaged equipment, logbooks stacked on shelves, a single oil lamp
sub_chapter_briefs.emotional_tone: Hyper-alert stillness; the particular silence of someone who has stopped breathing without noticing
sub_chapter_briefs.connects_to_book_arc: Delivers the inciting disruption of Stage 2 — the Call to Adventure arrives not as drama but as a faint, repeating tone on a frequency that should be dead, establishing the novel's central mystery and Mara's unique capacity to receive it

sub_chapter_briefs.title: Signal Architecture
sub_chapter_briefs.beat: Mara works through the night with graph paper and a mechanical pencil, mapping the signal's timing intervals, carrier stability, and modulation signature. Each technical conclusion tightens the knot in her chest: the carrier is too stable for atmospheric artifact, the repetition too precise for noise, the power too consistent for a battery rig. Someone has a grid. She writes it all in her private shorthand logbook.

sub_chapter_briefs.arc_beat: Stage 2 — Call to Adventure: the hero confirms the call is real and understands its full weight
sub_chapter_briefs.setting: Mara's radio room, deepening into the small hours — the oil lamp burning lower, her breath visible in the cold
sub_chapter_briefs.emotional_tone: Methodical excitement curdling into dread as each technical finding removes another innocent explanation
sub_chapter_briefs.connects_to_book_arc: Establishes Mara's signal-processing expertise as her heroic gift and grounds the novel's central premise in technical credibility; her logbook entry is the first instance of the ESCALATING THREAD — the written record that will draw the Reclamation Authority to her in later chapters

sub_chapter_briefs.title: What the Logbook Knows
sub_chapter_briefs.beat: Mara reads back what she has written and understands the danger with full clarity: a live grid 300–400 miles west means someone powerful enough to be a target, and anyone who knows about it becomes a target too. She tears the pages from the logbook, holds them over the lamp flame, and burns them. She watches the ash. Then she picks up the pencil and rewrites every word from memory — faster, neater, more complete.

sub_chapter_briefs.arc_beat: Stage 3 — Refusal of the Call: Mara destroys the evidence in fear, then immediately reverses herself, dramatizing the refusal and its failure in a single scene
sub_chapter_briefs.setting: Mara's radio room — the lamp guttering, ash on the floor, the logbook open to a fresh page
sub_chapter_briefs.emotional_tone: Fear giving way to compulsion; the specific self-knowledge of someone who understands their own weakness and acts on it anyway
sub_chapter_briefs.connects_to_book_arc: Dramatizes Stage 3's refusal as a gesture that collapses under the weight of who Mara is — she cannot unknow a signal; the rewritten logbook is the ESCALATING THREAD's second beat: the record now exists again, more complete than before, and will eventually be found

sub_chapter_briefs.title: Dani's Frequency
sub_chapter_briefs.beat: In the grey pre-dawn, Mara stops writing and sits with the logbook in her lap. Her mind goes to Dani — not the memory of his death but the memory of teaching him to read signal patterns on a Sunday afternoon, his finger tracing the waveform on a screen. She thinks: he would have heard it too. She thinks: he would have gone. She closes the logbook and does not sleep.

sub_chapter_briefs.arc_beat: Stage 3 — Refusal of the Call: the emotional underpinning of the refusal is revealed — it is not fear of the Reclamation Authority but fear of what going will cost, rooted in what staying cost her before
sub_chapter_briefs.setting: Mara's radio room into the kitchen — she moves to the window, watching the dead suburb go grey with early light
sub_chapter_briefs.emotional_tone: Grief worn smooth by seven years of handling; the quiet devastation of a person who has learned to carry loss without putting it down
sub_chapter_briefs.connects_to_book_arc: Plants the wound that the Hero's Journey will require Mara to confront — her guilt over Dani's death, her fear of choosing the signal over the people near her again; this is the interior stakes beneath the external quest

sub_chapter_briefs.title: The Knock
sub_chapter_briefs.beat: At first light, a knock at the farmhouse door — Tomás Reyes, on his courier route, stopping as he sometimes does to trade news for a meal. Mara lets him in, feeds him, says nothing about the signal. He notices the fresh ash on the floor near the lamp. He notices her hands are not still. He asks what she heard. She tells him it was nothing. He sits down, pours himself more water, and says he has time.
